case_title: Badal Murmu And Ors. v. State of West Bengal
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under section 148 and section 302 r/w section 149
offence_finally_established: culpable homicide not amounting to murder
neutral_facts: The accused and the victim were part of a community where a dispute arose over the theft of a hen by the victim. The accused called the victim to a meeting, where they tied him and his companion to trees and assaulted them with lathis. The victim died as a result of the injuries sustained during the assault. The accused were all present and participated in the beating, but no individual role was ascribed to any of them. The victim's wife and other witnesses observed the incident and provided accounts of the assault. The medical examination indicated that the victim's death was caused by the injuries sustained, but it was not clear which injury was fatal. The accused were armed with lathis and tangies, but the tangies were not used. The prosecution relied on eyewitness accounts and medical evidence to establish the assault and the victim's death.
